title: Abstract algebra I: groups
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn group theory with proofs: groups, subgroups and cyclic groups, permutation and symmetry groups, cosets and Lagrange's theorem, normal subgroups and quotient groups, homomorphisms and the isomorphism theorems, direct products and finite abelian groups, group actions and counting, conjugacy and the class equation, and the Sylow theorems, with computation in Python.
primary_reading: Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications by Thomas W. Judson (free online)

weeks.6: Homomorphisms and the first isomorphism theorem
weeks.7: The second and third isomorphism theorems
weeks.8: Direct products and finite abelian groups
weeks.10: Counting with group actions: Burnside's lemma
weeks.11: Conjugacy classes and the class equation
weeks.12: The Sylow theorems and groups of small order

blocks.deliverable: Prove that a supplied subset is a subgroup and find the orders of its elements.
Compute with permutations in cycle notation and apply Lagrange's theorem.
Identify a quotient group by means of a homomorphism.
Week 7 midterm; classify the abelian groups of a given order.
Count colorings up to symmetry with Burnside's lemma.
Use the Sylow theorems to show that no group of a given order is simple.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Symmetry casebook: find the symmetry groups of five objects (regular polygons, a cube and two patterns), identify each up to isomorphism with proofs, implement permutation multiplication and orbit counting in plain Python, and use Burnside's lemma to count the colorings of two of the objects.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
